title: Choose the consistency, index, and recovery boundary
description: Pick a workload, then assemble its read surface, write correctness control, and recovery mechanism. A fast API is not a complete contract unless all three decisions agree.

readPaths.label: Base table, eventual read
readPaths.detail: Lowest read-unit cost; a successful write might not be visible immediately.

readPaths.label: Base table, strong read
readPaths.detail: Reads the latest committed item by table key; not available on a GSI.

readPaths.label: GSI query, eventual read
readPaths.detail: Supports a different partition and sort key, with asynchronous index updates.

writeBoundaries.label: Unconditional write
writeBoundaries.detail: Overwrites the targeted item without checking its current business state.

writeBoundaries.label: Conditional write
writeBoundaries.detail: Atomically applies one item mutation only when its version or invariant still matches.

writeBoundaries.label: DynamoDB transaction
writeBoundaries.detail: Commits coordinated item actions as one ACID unit or cancels the whole request.

recoveries.label: Replica or stream only
recoveries.detail: Improves availability or change propagation, but can copy an accidental mutation.

recoveries.label: Occasional on-demand backup
recoveries.detail: Preserves named milestones but leaves gaps between backup times.

recoveries.label: Point-in-time recovery
recoveries.detail: Continuously captures recovery points and restores the selected time to a new table.

scenarios.label: Show a receipt immediately after checkout
scenarios.detail: An order and its payment ledger entry must commit together, then the receipt must show the committed order.
scenarios.requirement: Commit the order and ledger entry all-or-nothing, read the latest committed order by primary key, and retain a recovery point before an accidental application write.

rationale.readPath: The receipt is a read-your-write path. A strongly consistent base-table read can return the latest committed item; a GSI cannot provide that option.
rationale.writeBoundary: The order and ledger entry form one business operation. A transaction prevents one item from committing while the other fails.
rationale.recovery: PITR can restore the table to a selected second in a new table. A replica or stream can propagate the same accidental mutation instead of undoing it.

scenarios.safeOutcome: The checkout commits as one unit, the receipt reads the committed order from the authoritative key, and operators can restore a clean point into a new table.
scenarios.unsafeOutcome: A customer can observe a stale receipt, a split order/payment state, or no trustworthy rollback point after a destructive write.

scenarios.label: List open orders by status and time
scenarios.detail: Operators need a query that the base primary key does not support, and a few seconds of index lag is acceptable.
scenarios.requirement: Query open orders by status and creation time without scanning, protect each status transition from a stale worker, and recover from accidental bulk updates.

rationale.readPath: A GSI can use status as its partition key and creation time as its sort key. GSI reads are eventually consistent, which this dashboard explicitly tolerates.
rationale.writeBoundary: Each order transition is one-item state-machine work. A condition on the current status or version rejects a stale worker without paying for a multi-item transaction.
rationale.recovery: PITR covers an accidental bulk update. An index is another copy of selected attributes, not an independent backup.

scenarios.safeOutcome: The dashboard queries an index shaped for the access pattern, stale transition attempts fail atomically, and the source table has a restorable history.
scenarios.unsafeOutcome: The application may scan, demand unsupported strong reads from a GSI, overwrite a newer state, or discover that its secondary copy contains the same corruption.

scenarios.label: Reserve inventory without overselling
scenarios.detail: The displayed count may be slightly stale, but the authoritative mutation must never reduce stock below zero.
scenarios.requirement: Read the product by primary key, atomically decrement only when stock remains, and preserve recoverability from a bad deployment or operator command.

rationale.readPath: The UI may use the cheaper eventual base-table read because the displayed count is advisory. Read freshness alone cannot prevent a race.
rationale.writeBoundary: A conditional UpdateItem such as stock >= requested units is the authoritative no-oversell boundary. It evaluates atomically with the mutation.
rationale.recovery: PITR provides continuous recovery points and restores to a new table. It complements, rather than replaces, the conditional business invariant.

scenarios.safeOutcome: The UI remains inexpensive, concurrent reservations cannot cross the stock invariant, and an unrelated destructive write remains recoverable.
scenarios.unsafeOutcome: Treating a pre-read as a lock can oversell under concurrency, while a replica or stream can faithfully reproduce the bad state.
